about.title: Colfax Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Colfax residents often rely on nearby regional hospitals and clinics along the I-80 corridor for care, and when something goes wrong during treatment, families are left with hard questions and few local resources to turn to. Medical malpractice cases are different from most injury claims — California's MICRA law requires a qualified medical expert to review the care given, a strict notice period before any lawsuit, and firm deadlines that don't bend for confusion or grief. A bad result isn't automatically malpractice; the law asks whether the provider deviated from an accepted standard of care. For Colfax residents unsure whether what happened to them or a loved one crosses that line, we offer a free, no-obligation case review to help you understand the details and explain your options plainly, without pressure or guesswork.

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Strict and Layered
items.desc: California generally gives one year from discovering the harm, capped at three years from the injury itself, plus a mandatory 90-day pre-suit notice — missing any of these can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a poor medical outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California law typically requires a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was violated.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises
items.desc: MICRA sets a statutory limit on non-economic damages that increases annually, so understanding the current cap and how it applies matters when evaluating a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim after treatment in Colfax?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. A required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider also affects your timeline, so it's worth getting a claim reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does a bad outcome from surgery or treatment automatically mean malpractice occurred?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, not simply that the result was disappointing or unexpected. A qualified medical expert is almost always needed to make that determination.

items.question: Colfax is a small community — does that affect where a malpractice claim gets handled?
items.answer: Not in terms of the legal standards, which apply the same way statewide under MICRA. However, Placer County court procedures and where treatment occurred can affect logistics, which is something our team can walk you through.

items.question: Is there a cost to find out if I have a case?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
